responses.content:
There is no credible evidence to suggest that Albert Einstein failed math in school. In fact, there are records of his academic achievements and participation in educational programs during his early years.

Einstein's parents enrolled him in a private Jewish school in Munich, Germany when he was seven years old, and later transferred him to the Luitpold Gymnasium in Munich, where he excelled academically. He continued to attend school there until he was 15 years old.

At the University of Zurich, Einstein studied physics with Wilhelm Konrad Dorbach, but he did not focus on mathematics as his major. Instead, he focused on philosophy and physics. It wasn't until later in his academic career that he took up physics full-time.

Einstein's academic record at university was marked by his exceptional abilities and achievements, including winning a scholarship to attend the Swiss Federal Polytechnic University (now ETH Zurich) as an exchange student from 1896 to 1900.

It's worth noting that Einstein's education and academic background have been extensively documented and verified through various sources, including his own writings and biographies.
